notes.title: Demo Build - Update 0.1.5
notes.content:
Several performance improvements to the Steam Demo build.

In the past months I've been focusing on performance improvements to address some of the issues players were having on low/medium and high setups. Framerates should now be improved on all presets, especially allowing more options to be tweaked for low and medium setups. I've also completely reworked the saving system with more performant autosaving to reduce framedrops.

(!) Note: If you're playing on an older save from 0.1.4 or earlier, you'll have to toggle between the quality presets or reset to default video settings to apply the new changes correctly.

(!) Note: If you're playing on an older save from 0.1.4 or earlier the autosaving will still default to the less performant saving method to ensure backwards compatibility. Fresh saves use the new system.

Changes:
- Reworked Low / Medium / High quality presets
- Added a Global Illumination option to turn Lumen off completely on lower end hardware
- Added TSR / TAA / FXAA / NO AA Anti Aliasing options to the video settings menu
- Added and optimized CSM / VSM Shadow settings
- Added and optimized Off / SSR / Lumen options for Reflections
- Added Texture resolution settings
- Added a new Brightness setting slider to brighten dark or hard to see areas on certain screens
- Added ceiling lights to darker areas in the lower level to help with navigation
- Reduced and cleaned up files sizes, materials, engine settings, redundant code and more
- Optimized clouds and other elements in the environment
- Optimized and reworked performance intensive blueprints
- Optimized and reworked auto-saving to reduce hitches on new saves
- Changed the default Steam Deck preset to Low for 60 FPS (Medium runs at 30-40 FPS)

Bugs:
- Fixed an issue where setting Global Illumination to Medium made certain areas in the game too dark and hard to see. Medium (Lumen) is now the default for increased performance.
- Fixed an issue where screen fade transitions would not cover the full screen on 21:9 monitors
- Fixed an issue where the lowest mouse sensitivity would still be too sensitive. Increased the mouse sensitivity slider range for more control.

Updated Minimum Requirements:
- GTX 1050 Ti / 4GB VRAM for 60 FPS on Low settings
- DirectX Version 12 is required
- Integrated Intel GPUs are not supported

If you had performance issues before, or an older graphics card, let me know if these new options made a difference on your machine. Sharing your preset (low/medium/high), your FPS (displayed in the video settings menu) and your graphics card with me would be very helpful.

I'll try to further improve the performance as development progresses.

notes.title: Demo Build - Update 0.1.4
notes.content:
Several smaller fixes to the Steam Demo build.

Bugs:
 Fixed any strangely rotated and broken elements in the tower puzzle
(caused by a float value of 0.000001 after a certain number of game save/loads)
 Implemented a broader fix to prevent future float value issues
 Fixed a collision issue where the player could get stuck on top of a barrier
 Fixed a bug where the player would maintain movement speed on pause
 
Steam Deck:
 Fixed a bug where the Fullscreen setting on Steam Deck would warp the resolution and aspect ratio incorrectly displaying the game with black borders  
Known issues – to be fixed:
 Overall performance and compatibility issues
 Steam Deck resetting progress causes the menu and game input to stop working. The touchscreen does work, quitting and restarting solves the issue for now (have not reproduced this issue yet)

notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions
notes.content:
Hey Steam!

Thanks for following along, wishlisting the game and sharing my announcement! With your help, the game has managed to hit nearly 1000 (988) wishlists in the first two weeks.

On top of this, I've felt the support from fellow developers and the Thinky Games community:

 Alexander Bruce quote re-tweeted my game
 Jonathan Blow streamed the game on his Twitch channel
 Thinky Games covered and added the game to their database

Shout-out to Davor Hunski (The Talos Principle), Albert Shih (Superliminal), Elyot Grant (Islands of Insight), Patrick Traynor (Patrick's Parabox), Le Slo (Alephant), Matthew VanDevander (Taiji), Alan Hazelden (Draknek), Nozomu (Robot Detour), Thomas Mackinnon (THE CORRIDOR), Tad Cordle (Sensorium) and many more for play-testing early builds of the game.
[hr][/hr]
This is my first devlog after over a year of development. As a developer, I'm a bit torn on what I should or shouldn't share in terms of game design/mechanics. The game is all about rule discovery and mastering mechanics over time, I don't want to spoil or ruin that experience for you.

Anything that might be considered a spoiler, like this [spoiler]spoiler example[/spoiler], will be marked as a spoiler. If you want to go in blind, [spoiler]don't hover over these[/spoiler]!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45292736/77bfa9e8d9989669ab48f9dfefa9322cf88e6557.png
I'll be posting a devlog every month or so, depending on my schedule. I'd love to share interesting bits and pieces of my process along the way. What would you prefer to see (or not see) in a devlog for a puzzle game that's in active development?
[hr][/hr]
Let's start simple by giving you an overview of where I'm at:

 Late 2022: I joined a game-jam that triggered the idea to hyperfocus on the button mechanic
 February 2023: I developed a rough prototype next to my work as an architectural engineer
 March 2023: I reduced my engineering hours to a minimum to make time for game development
 May 2023: I applied for the Astra Fellowship grant but didn't make it through final selections
 July 2023: I continued to improve my early demo and asked for advice from fellow developers
 October 2023: I became increasingly unhappy in my engineering job and quit (not recommended)
 Late 2023: I continued to self-fund pre-production and prepared pitches to find funding
 April 2024: I sent in my pitch to the Dutch equivalent of Indie Fund (a dev friendly initiative)
 May 2024: I succesfully received funding from Midgame Fund to fund my project full-time
 June 2024: I quietly showcased a build of the game at the INDIGO showcase in Utrecht (NL)
 August 2024: I focused on improving the game's visuals, trailer and store-page materials
 November 2024: I announced the game and published the Steam store-page

My next milestone? – Work towards a playable Steam demo!

I'm also focusing on production: I've got new mechanics to explore, puzzles to design and levels to tie together. Significant amounts of my time go into iteration – which I believe is worth it in the long run. I prefer quality over quantity, only the most interesting designs should make it into the final game.

More on that later. Let me know what you'd like to see?
[hr][/hr]
For now, let's wrap up this somewhat lengthy devlog with a short FAQ:

(Q) How long will the game be?
(A) 3~4 hours is the current estimated playtime

(Q) What are the target platforms?
(A) Windows (PC) only at first, potentially Steam Deck and Linux/MacOS after

(Q) How do you design puzzles using nothing but buttons?
(A)[spoiler]Each of the various button types has its own hidden ruleset[/spoiler]

(Q) What will it cost?
(A) It depends on the content, but likely somewhere between $9,99 ~ $19,99

(Q) Is the music inspired by Westworld?
(A) Not intentionally, I sent my composer Beth's Story (The Queen's Gambit) as a reference

[hr][/hr]
That's all for now. If you're curious about specific aspects of the game, feel free to ask me anything!

Thanks for reading,
-Tim (Frycandle)
